Dearborn is a city of about 110,000, Michigan’s seventh largest, and it is three cities in one: the east side along Michigan Avenue and Warren, dense, walkable, and home to one of the largest and most established Arab American communities in the United States; the west side around downtown West Dearborn and Ford’s world headquarters; and the industrial south, the Rouge complex and the rail and truck corridors that serve it. Each produces its own injuries.

sections.heading: What is different about a Dearborn claim

c.v: Before Michigan’s 2019 no-fault reform, Dearborn motorists, like many drivers across metropolitan Detroit, faced high automobile insurance costs. After a crash, the amount of coverage available depends on the policies involved, making uninsured and underinsured motorist protection important to review. Your own no-fault insurer pays your medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107), or the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan does if no household policy applies (MCL 500.3172, capped at $250,000); the claim against the at-fault driver for pain and suffering requires a threshold injury (MCL 500.3135) and is worth no more than the insurance available unless you carry your own uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. We review every policy in the household before we value a Dearborn claim. See our

The City of Dearborn maintains its own streets, sidewalks, parks, and buildings, and operates its own police, fire, and EMS; Wayne County maintains the county roads; MDOT maintains Michigan Avenue, Ford Road, Telegraph, the Southfield Freeway, and I-94; SMART runs the buses; Dearborn Public Schools runs the school buses. A qualifying highway or municipal sidewalk defect claim generally requires written notice within 120 days under MCL 691.1404, including qualifying claims involving MDOT-maintained roads. Notice for state highway-defect claims must be filed with the Court of Claims as required by that statute. Crashes involving city, school district, or SMART vehicles may support claims under the governmental motor vehicle exception, MCL 691.1405, when injuries result from negligent operation of government-owned vehicles. Certain tort claims against SMART also require written notice within 60 days under MCL 124.419. Injuries caused by qualifying dangerous conditions in city-owned public buildings may fall within MCL 691.1406, subject to its requirements, including 120-day written notice.
The 19th District and the Third Circuit.

Claims up to $25,000, including mini tort claims for vehicle damage (MCL 500.3135(3)(e), up to $3,000), are filed in the 19th District Court at 16077 Michigan Avenue, a few blocks from our office. Injury suits over $25,000 go to the Third Judicial Circuit Court at the Coleman A. Young Municipal Center in Detroit; wrongful death estates (MCL 600.2922) and minors’ settlements (MCR 2.420) to the Wayne County Probate Court in the same building. Where a defendant lives or does business outside Wayne County, venue may be available elsewhere (MCL 600.1629).

Corewell Health Dearborn Hospital (formerly Beaumont Dearborn), on Oakwood Boulevard, is a verified Level II trauma center serving the city. Henry Ford Medical Center Fairlane, the Level I trauma centers at Detroit Receiving Hospital and Henry Ford Hospital, Garden City Hospital, and Corewell Health Taylor also serve patients from Dearborn and surrounding communities.

Dearborn is a city where a large share of residents speak Arabic at home, and an injury claim is hard enough in a first language. ATLAW serves clients in English, Arabic, French, Mandarin, Urdu, and Spanish.

faqs.question: How many crashes happen in Dearborn each year?

answer.v: In 2024, Dearborn recorded 3,326 traffic crashes, with 1,113 people injured and four killed, according to Michigan Traffic Crash Facts. Wayne County as a whole recorded 50,355 crashes, 16,458 people injured, and 177 deaths that year.

faqs.question: I was hit crossing Michigan Avenue or Warren. Who pays?

answer.v: A pedestrian struck by a motor vehicle is covered by no-fault: your own auto policy if you have one, then a household member’s, then the insurer of the vehicle’s owner, then its driver, then the Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3115). Your pain-and-suffering claim against the driver requires a threshold injury and depends on the driver’s coverage and your own UM/UIM. See our

faqs.question: I was hurt at the Rouge or another Dearborn plant. Can I sue?

answer.v: Not your employer, in most cases; workers’ compensation is the exclusive remedy. You can sue a third party whose negligence caused the injury, a contractor, a vendor’s driver, or an equipment manufacturer, and pursue both claims at once.

faqs.question: I fell on a Dearborn sidewalk. Who is responsible?

answer.v: The City of Dearborn may be responsible for a qualifying sidewalk defect under MCL 691.1402a, subject to governmental-immunity rules and generally a 120-day written notice requirement. Dearborn also imposes maintenance responsibilities on adjacent property owners, but whether an owner may be held liable depends on the specific circumstances and applicable law.
